source_acquisition.search_note: The project page https://omniverifier.github.io/ has the exact paper title and explicitly links https://github.com/Cominclip/OmniVerifier as Code; gh repo view confirms the exact ICLR 2026 title, default branch main, and homepage https://arxiv.org/abs/2510.13804. The recursive GitHub tree contains data-construction, inference, evaluation, SAM 2.1, and FLUX inpainting files (for example data/method1/step1_image_recaption.py, data/method2/step6_inpainting.py, sequential_omniverifier_tts.py, and viverbench_eval_rule_based.py), but no plot*, figure*, visual*, table*, notebook, TeX/TikZ/PGF, SVG, or Figure 1–10/Table 1–7 export source. The automated inventory candidate black-forest-labs/flux is a cited inpainting baseline rather than an author repository. corpus/visual_sources/iclr-2026-4e1d7790186d/ is absent, so no exact public visual source file is recorded.

paper_style.palette_strategy: Black/white tables use thin rules, bold model/ours values, and gray improvement or Mean Round fills. Figure 3 uses red/yellow/teal/blue training-data roles; Figure 4 uses three blue capability levels; Figures 5/7 reuse gray UMM, pale-blue verifier, and red stage labels; qualitative figures use gray/cream prompt cards and full-color generated thumbnails.
paper_style.vector_raster_mix: Figure 3, Figure 4, Figure 7, and all tables are predominantly PDF vector. Figures 1, 2, 5, 6, 8, 9, and 10 combine vector cards/text/arrows with embedded JPEG/bitmap thumbnails. Captions and surrounding paper text are vector.
paper_style.style_consistency: Nimbus Roman No9 L and Computer Modern math are stable in body, captions, and tables; TeX Gyre Pagella card text and DejaVu Sans chart/diagram text form local visual systems. Gray containers, black rules, pale-blue verifier/capability accents, and red stage labels recur, but internal figure text ranges from roughly 3–10 pt and series color semantics are not globally redundant.

figures.label: Figure 1

caption.text: Figure 1: ViVerBench Overview. ViVerBench has a 1:1 ratio of true to false answers; here, we show only the false ones to better highlight data difficulty.

color.semantic_mapping: Gray category bars and card borders encode hierarchy; red words mark prompt/image mismatch; thumbnail colors are content.

encodings.y: none; category groups and stacked task cards
encodings.color: category hierarchy and red mismatch words; thumbnail content color
encodings.shape: rounded cards, category bars, and embedded example thumbnails
encodings.facet: Concept Existence, Object Relationship, World Dynamics, Image Annotation, State Value Evaluation, STEM
encodings.text: task prompts, False answers, explanations, and category/task labels

figures.data_and_statistics: Benchmark overview with 16 representative false examples; no statistical marks, sample denominator, aggregation, uncertainty, or inferential test. The 1:1 true/false ratio is stated in the caption, while task-level sample counts are in the body/Appendix A.
figures.evidence_relation: Introduction visual-outcome verification gap -> §3.1 benchmark taxonomy and curation -> Figure 1 task/example interface -> Table 1 per-task accuracy -> Appendix A complete task definitions.
design_strengths: Six category groups make 16 heterogeneous tasks scannable on one page.
Prompt, answer, explanation, and thumbnail are colocated, exposing the verification target.
Red mismatch terms make a false case concrete rather than leaving difficulty abstract.
design_weaknesses: Sixteen cards create high density and small text/images are hard to read at normal scale.
Examples are selected exemplars, not a distribution or success-rate estimate.
Red emphasis has no shape or typographic redundancy and fades in grayscale.
figures.reusable_pattern: Use a category-to-task-card grid with prompt, answer, explanation, and example image to introduce a benchmark interface; add per-category counts and sampling rules when it must carry quantitative claims.

evidence.label: p.4 Figure 1 six category groups, 16 task cards, thumbnails, and caption

cross_object_system.visual_narrative: Figure 1 exposes the benchmark gap through false-case cards; Table 1 quantifies it with advanced/Random/Human/base/ours anchors; Figure 2 gives the data-construction interface; Figure 3/4 turn transfer curves into a capability mechanism; Figure 5 connects verification to iterative image editing; Figure 6 and Table 2 show qualitative and aggregate TTS results; Figure 7 and Table 3 isolate parallel versus sequential topology and scores; Appendix Tables 4–7 and Figures 8–10 add transfer, efficiency, stronger-verifier, success, failure, and world-modeling boundaries.
cross_object_system.caption_system: All 17 numbered objects have nearby captions. Figure 1 states its false-example/ratio setting and Figure 9 states a backbone limitation; most other captions are naming-only. Captions rarely define colors, uncertainty, sample size, metric scale, or aggregation, so independent interpretation usually requires body text.
cross_object_system.table_header_system: Tables 1–3 use two-level category/metric headers; Tables 4, 5, and 7 use single-level headers; Table 6 uses two-level benchmark-group headers. Model/backbone/verifier/strategy and Overall roles are visible, while abbreviations, units, round definitions, and delta semantics often remain in prose.
cross_object_system.method_result_ablation_link: Figure 2 links data-construction branches to training input; Figure 3 probes four one-task RL settings and Figure 4 summarizes transfer as capability layers rather than component deletion; Table 1 evaluates the trained verifier; Figure 5–7 and Tables 2–3 connect the verifier loop to generation/TTS; Tables 6–7 add round and verifier slices. No seed/uncertainty or compute-normalized ablation closes the chain.
cross_object_system.main_appendix_link: Figures 1–7 and Tables 1–3 establish the benchmark→training→TTS main line. Appendix Tables 4–7 expand transfer/efficiency/strong-verifier comparisons, Figure 8 adds success cases, Figure 9 shows error accumulation, and Figure 10 demonstrates world-modeling interactions. Several appendix objects are not explicitly numbered in the main text, and adverse/qualitative evidence remains mostly descriptive.
cross_object_system.typography_consistency: PDF body/caption/table fonts are consistent Nimbus Roman with math fonts. Figure 1/2/5/8/9 cards use TeX Gyre Pagella and Figure 3/4 use DejaVu Sans; these local systems are coherent but not unified in size or weight. The smallest tables and qualitative cards need zoom to read.
cross_object_system.color_consistency: Gray cards/containers, black arrows/rules, pale-blue verifier/capability accents, and red stage labels recur across diagrams. Figure 3 is the only stable multi-series palette; Table 4–6 gray fills mark ours/improvement/efficiency. Figure 3 series and Figure 9 yellowing depend on color more than the rest.

most_reusable_patterns: Figure 2 two-branch data construction pipeline with explicit true/false schema.
Figure 3 fixed-palette small multiples plus Figure 4 capability ring for transfer-to-mechanism narration.
Figure 5/7 matched state-loop/process topologies for verifier editing and parallel/sequential contrast.
Table 1–3 grouped headers and base/ours or baseline/intervention rows, with Table 6 quality×Mean Round joint decision surface.
Figure 9 complete failure trajectory retaining edit prompts and successive outputs.
highest_value_objects: Figure 1 gives the highest-density scope and error-interface overview.
Table 1 is the main model/human/chance/base/OmniVerifier comparison surface.
Figure 3 and Figure 4 provide the transfer-to-capability mechanism bridge.
Figure 5 with Tables 2–3 connects verifier mechanics to generation results and a matched TTS comparison.
